dataset.name: freMTPL2freq
dataset.target: observed: the policy filed at least one claim

missing_field_check.description: dropping a required numeric field must block the recommendation

limitations: freMTPL2 carries no insurer accept/reject ground truth: the target is the real observed fact "the policy filed at least one claim". Quality is therefore a discrimination proxy of the final risk score against an observed outcome, not a measure of an acceptance policy.
The eleven agents are deterministic by default (no provider call): token and dollar totals are legitimately zero unless an LLM skill is enabled with a provider key.

Latency is measured after a warm-up pass (see ``_warm_up``) so the first combination does not pay the one-off model and import cost; the values are wall-clock milliseconds on a shared machine and carry the usual jitter.
Missing-field robustness is a fail-closed property of the mandatory intake agent: it is identical across combinations and is therefore reported once, not per combination.

Across the 256 evaluated combinations these Pareto axes take a single value and therefore cannot discriminate between them: metrics.quality.roc_auc.point, metrics.cost.usd_per_case, metrics.tokens.per_case.

The quality axis is identical for every combination: the final risk score IS the mandatory risk agent score, and the optional agents change the decision label without changing the score ranking. Quality separates nothing in this case -- that is a property of the pipeline, not of the observed target.

Decision stability is quantised over 100 measured noisy decisions, so the whole spread between the best and worst combination is 1 decision(s) out of 100; a difference that small sits inside the published bootstrap interval and is not by itself a reliable ranking signal.
